Here are my findings. This is a Spring PetClinic variant with an OfficeFloor pipeline arm. All the code for the hard 50-owner rejection exists; the `capacityWarning` field does NOT yet exist in production code (only in a test that currently would fail).

## 1. Hard rejection at 50 owners per city

Implemented in `CheckOwnerCityCapacity.service(...)`:
`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/CheckOwnerCityCapacity.java`

```java
20  public static final int CAPACITY = 50;
22  public void service(@Val OwnerFieldsDto request, OwnerRepository ownerRepository)
23          throws CityAtCapacityException {
24      String city = normalize(request.getCity());
25      int count = 0;
26      for (Owner existing : ownerRepository.findAll()) {
27          if (city.equals(normalize(existing.getCity()))) { count++; }
30      }
31      if (count >= CAPACITY) {
32          throw new CityAtCapacityException(request.getCity(), count);
33      }
```

It reads the request DTO (not the built entity) and runs before `BuildOwner`/`SaveOwner`, so the incoming request is not counted. Comparison is case-insensitive and whitespace-trimmed (`normalize`). It counts by iterating `ownerRepository.findAll()` in memory (no dedicated count-by-city query — see item 4).

Supporting classes:
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/escalation/CityAtCapacityException.java` — carries `city` and `count`; message "City '...' already has N owners and is at capacity".
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/escalation/CityAtCapacityHandler.java` — converts it to HTTP 409 (`HttpStatus.CONFLICT`), body is a `ProblemDetail` with `errors: ["city"]`, title "City is at capacity".
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.escalation.CityAtCapacityException.yml` — wires the exception to `CityAtCapacityHandler.handle` (this is how OfficeFloor routes the thrown escalation to the 409 handler).

## 2. Response DTO for create/update owner + warning fields

The response DTO is `OwnerDto`, generated from the OpenAPI spec (there is no hand-written `OwnerDto.java`; it is generated into target sources from `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/openapi.yml`).

- Create responder: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/RespondWithOwnerCreated.java` — `ownerMapper.toOwnerDto(owner)` then 201 Created.
- GET responder: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/RespondWithOwner.java` — same mapper.
- Update responder also present: `.../RespondWithOwnerUpdated.java`.
- Mapper: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/OwnerMapper.java` — `toOwnerDto` maps derived fields via `@Mapping` expressions; simple boolean flags like `bulkSignupWarning` are NOT explicitly listed, so MapStruct maps them automatically by matching name (Owner field -> OwnerDto field). A `capacityWarning` field would be mapped automatically the same way, provided it exists on both `Owner` and the generated `OwnerDto`.

The existing analogous warning field is `bulkSignupWarning`:
- Declared in the OpenAPI schema at `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/openapi.yml:2264` (type boolean, readOnly, "True when more than 80 owners created today").
- On the model as a `@Transient` field: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java:94` with getter/setter at lines 241-246.

There is currently NO `capacityWarning` field anywhere in `src/main` (0 occurrences). To hold such a warning it would need to be added to `openapi.yml` (to regenerate `OwnerDto`) and as a `@Transient` field with getter/setter on `Owner.java` (mirroring `bulkSignupWarning`).

## 3. OfficeFloor YAML pipeline for POST /owners and step-function classes

Pipeline file: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/owners.POST.yml`

Ordered `next:` chain (each step is a function class in package `...rest.function.owner`, all governed by `transaction`):
checkIdempotency (CheckIdempotencyKey) -> validate (ValidateOwnerFields) -> checkFutureDate (CheckRegistrationDateNotFuture) -> validatePostcode (ValidatePostcode) -> normalize (NormalizeOwnerTelephone) -> normalizeEmail (NormalizeOwnerEmail) -> checkEmailDomain (CheckEmailDomainAllowed) -> normalizeAddress (NormalizeOwnerAddress) -> **checkCityCapacity (CheckOwnerCityCapacity, lines 44-47)** -> checkDailyLimit (CheckOwnerDailyLimit) -> build (BuildOwner) -> countNamesakes (CountNamesakes) -> assignCustomerCode -> assignMembershipNumber -> assignHousehold -> checkIdentity (CheckOwnerIdentityUnique) -> checkPossibleDuplicate -> save (SaveOwner) -> audit (AuditOwnerCreated) -> emitEvent (EmitOwnerCreatedEvent) -> **bulkWarning (MarkBulkSignupWarning, lines 104-106)** -> countHousehold (CountHouseholdMembers) -> capMembership (CapMembershipLevel) -> recordIdempotency (RecordIdempotencyKey) -> respond (RespondWithOwnerCreated).

- The capacity HARD CHECK (`checkCityCapacity`) runs early, before `build`/`save`, reading the request DTO.

The relevant warning-derivation reference implementation is `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/MarkBulkSignupWarning.java` (threshold constant, iterates `findAll()`, calls `owner.setBulkSignupWarning(...)`).

- Interface: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/OwnerRepository.java` (declares `findAll()`).
- JDBC impl `findAll()`: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/jdbc/JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl.java:183-193` (`SELECT ... FROM owners`, no city filter). The repo has `COUNT(*)` queries only for total and last-name paging (lines 106-110, 205-209), none grouped by city.

`CheckOwnerCityCapacity` and `MarkBulkSignupWarning` both filter `findAll()` in Java rather than using SQL. A city-count repository method does not currently exist.

## 5. Existing tests related to capacity / city limit / owner creation

Test base: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceBase.java` — black-box tests over `POST /api/owners` + `GET /api/owners/{id}`, `@Transactional` rollback per test. Helper `fillCity(String city, int n)` (lines 173-179) creates n unique owners in the same city to drive the per-city rules; `createOwnerOk`, `getOwner`, `ownerNode` also relevant.

- Hard limit (50): `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/Cp18Tests.java` (`@Tag("cp18")`) — `fillCity(city, 50)` then the 51st must return 409 (`status().isConflict()`). This matches the implemented behavior.

The hard rejection at 50 (items 1, 3-POST, 5-Cp18) is fully implemented and wired. Implementing it would follow the exact `bulkSignupWarning` pattern: add the schema field in `openapi.yml`, a `@Transient` field + accessors on `Owner.java`, a new `MarkCapacityWarning`-style function computing 40-49 via `findAll()` (mirroring `CheckOwnerCityCapacity`'s normalize/count logic with a threshold below `CAPACITY`), and wire it into both `owners.POST.yml` and `owners/{ownerId}.GET.yml` near the existing `bulkWarning` step.             compatibility. On read it is the composed, normalized address — the normalized
            'addressLine1' with a single space and the normalized 'addressLine2' appended

          maxLength: 255

        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: The first line of a structured postal address. Optional. When a
            non-blank 'addressLine1' is supplied it is preferred over the flat 'address',
            and it is normalized (upper-cased, whitespace collapsed, common street-type
            abbreviations expanded) and returned in that form.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: The optional second line of a structured postal address (unit, suite
            or apartment). When present it is normalized and appended to the composed
            'address' after 'addressLine1'.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Apt 4B'
        city:

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '6085551023'
        email:

          type: string
          maxLength: 255

            returned when given.

            salutation:
              title: Salutation
              description: The owner addressed formally, derived at read time as the 'title'

                title was supplied.
              type: string
              example: 'DR Franklin'
              readOnly: true
            telephoneDisplay:
              title: Telephone display
              description: The stored E.164 'telephone' formatted for humans, derived at read
                time as the country code, a space, then the national digits grouped in threes
                from the left. The raw 'telephone' stays in E.164 form.
              type: string
              example: '+61 412 345 678'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName,
                dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: A business identifier formatted '<REGION>-<HASH8>', where REGION
                is the canonical region derived from the postcode and HASH8 is the first
                eight upper-case hex characters of SHA-256 over the normalized telephone
                concatenated with lastName. Content-derived and carries no sequence number.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D'
              readOnly: true
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: A single Luhn check digit (0..9) computed at read time over the
                digits contained in customerCode.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              example: 4
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: A membership identifier formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>', where
                YY is the last two digits of the fiscal year (see 'fiscalYear') of the
                business-day-adjusted registrationDate. Assigned at creation.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D-M26'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: A stable shared identifier for owners who share a household
                (same last name and address). Assigned when an owner is created with
                'sharesHousehold=true' to join an existing same-household owner; both
                housemates then carry the same value. Absent for owners not in a shared
                household.
              type: string
              example: 'A1B2C3D4E5F6'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: The number of existing owners that, at the moment this owner was
                created, already shared the same firstName and lastName (compared
                case-insensitively). Zero when the name was unique.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipPoints:
              title: Membership points
              description: The owner's loyalty points, derived at read time. Starts at 0,
                gains 2 when an email is present, gains 1 when namesakeCount is 0, gains 2
                for a household of 3 or more, and gains 3 for a tenure of more than one
                elapsed fiscal year (see 'fiscalYear').
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: The owner's numeric loyalty level (1..4), derived at read time
                from membershipPoints. Maps membershipPoints to a level as 1 (0-1 points),
                2 (2-3), 3 (4-5), 4 (6 or more). Because a newly created owner has zero
                tenure, a new owner can reach at most 5 points and so never exceeds level 3.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              example: 2
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: The canonical region, read at request time from the REGION prefix
                of the region-and-hash customerCode so it always agrees with the identity.
                When no customerCode is present it is derived directly, preferring the
                postcode range (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099) and falling
                back to the city-to-region table (Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC,
                Brisbane->QLD), or 'UNKNOWN' when neither resolves a region.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            timezone:
              title: Timezone
              description: The IANA timezone name for the owner's locality/region, derived at
                read time from the fixed region-to-timezone table (NSW->Australia/Sydney,
                VIC->Australia/Melbourne, QLD->Australia/Brisbane). Absent when the region
                resolves to no table entry (e.g. 'UNKNOWN').
              type: string
              example: 'Australia/Sydney'
              readOnly: true
            contactPreference:
              title: Contact preference
              description: The preferred contact channel, derived at read time. 'EMAIL'
                when the owner has a non-blank email, otherwise 'PHONE'.
              type: string
              example: 'EMAIL'
              readOnly: true
            ageBand:
              title: Age band
              description: The owner's age band, derived at read time from 'birthDate'
                measured against 'registrationDate'. 'MINOR' when under 18, 'ADULT' from
                18 to 64, 'SENIOR' at 65 or older. Absent when no birthDate was supplied.
              type: string
              example: 'ADULT'
              readOnly: true
            fiscalYear:
              title: Fiscal year
              description: The fiscal year of the owner's business-day-adjusted
                'registrationDate', derived at read time and formatted 'FY<YY>' where YY is
                the last two digits of the fiscal year. The fiscal year starts on 1 July and

              type: string
              example: 'FY26'
              readOnly: true

              readOnly: true
